key_insight: DecisionRank aims to transfer a generative language model’s ranking knowledge into a decision model that scores candidates directly, avoiding autoregressive decoding. Its central idea is item-space on-policy distillation, bridging the gap between ranked document sequences and first-token scores.
problem_solved: The teacher expresses preferences as an ordered sequence of document IDs, while the student ranks documents using scores at the first-token position. These different output formats make knowledge transfer challenging.
method: Use a generative language model’s ranked document-ID sequences as the source of ranking knowledge.
Apply item-space on-policy distillation to connect sequence-based teacher preferences with the student’s scoring formulation.
Train a decision-model reranker to order documents directly from first-token scores rather than generate a ranking autoregressively.
impact: This approach targets lower-latency reranking while retaining ranking knowledge from generative language models. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no benchmark results, so accuracy and speed gains cannot be quantified.
visual_elements: Teacher–student diagram: generative ranked list → item-space distillation → decision-model scores.
Output comparison: ordered document IDs versus a document-score bar chart.
Inference flow comparison: sequential token decoding versus direct scoring and sorting.
Document cards showing how candidate scores determine the final ranking.
paper_title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
paper_authors: Yanran Wu, Dian Yu, Chongyang Bai, Jieyi Zhang, Rui Liu
